newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates steady but mkt cautious.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates steady but mkt cautious.

text.p: * Volume down to 9.606 bln from 13.632 bln pesos
Philippine interbank call loan rates were firm at an average of 10.03125 percent on Friday but banks see interest rates rising in the next few weeks because of tax remittances, dealer said.
"Next week it's going to be net out," a foreign bank dealer said, adding that projections showed banks could be short of five billion pesos on a net basis.

This takes into account an outflow of 25 billion pesos in tax remmitances to the government, inflow of 10 billion pesos of incoming deposits for tax payments and another inflow of 10 billion pesos from the maturities of floating rate treasury notes, the dealer said.
"Banks are very cautious of liquidity," he added.
Done rates were in the same band from 10.25 to 10.03125 percent in a market with 23 lenders and 16 borrowers.
In the secondary market, there was little trading as banks anticipated a further rise in interest rates at the regular weekly Treasury bill auction on Monday.
"Most are sellers in all tenors," a big bank dealer said, since banks want to dispose their old, low-interest bills.
A Reuters poll of seven financial institutions gave offer rates of 10.15/10.35 percent on the three-month bills; 10.525/10.65 on the six months; and 11.05/11.25 on the one-year bills.
